This method is used to 
 determine the alkalinity of water imparted by the bicarbonate, carbonate, 
 and hydroxide components of natural or treated water supply.

The first draft was initiated by chemist Amany 
 Mohammed Mohammed EL-Hasanieen; reviewed by department director chemist: 
 Zakia Soltan; revised by quality control chemist: Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel and 
 accepted by Eng. Awad M. Fatthy; Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.

Determination of bicarbonate, carbonate, hydroxide and total alkalinity by titration 
 with standrad solution of a strong mineral acid by means of color.

Residual chlorine affects the indicator color response and can be overcome by 
 the addition of minimum volumes of sodium 
 thiosulfate. Finely divided calcium carbonate and magnesium hydroxide which may 
 cause a fading end point can removed by filtration through fine filter paper.

Titration of the sample with 0.02 N 
 HCL using ph.ph. and M.O. as indicators.

For best results, samples should be collected in 
 polyethylene or pyrex bottles, the alkalinity determination should be 
 performed within 1day. Keep samples in a cool place; avoid agitation and 
 contact with air if storage is required.

The reagent used 
 must be of sufficiently high purity to permit its use without lessening 
 the accuracy of determination.

Water used for this method 
 shall be free from carbon dioxide.

Samples containing free 
 available residual chlorine and low alkalinity require pretreatment prior to 
 examination.

Select an appropriate buret 
 capacity so that the sample uses at least 20-30% of the total buret capacity, 
 insuring volumetric accuracy.
Carbon Dioxidefree distilled water- Remove CO2 by boiling 15 minutes and cooling to room temperature just prior to use.

Sodium Carbonate Solution 0.05 N- Dry 3-5 g Na2CO3 
 at 250C for 4 h and cool in a desicator. Weigh 2.5 0.2 g, transfer to a 1-L 
 volumetric flask, fill flask to the mark with distilled water, and dissolve 
 and mix reagent. Don't keep longer than 1 week.

Introduction
